contexts.text: (His mouth was) a maw in which there stood up teeth in a row.
Three-headed dogs seen, all with a horrible maw.
He had cords which he stretched forth, and swallowed...

The Hell there is like a maw with gullets which are extensible; and, as soon as they came, it extended its maw by bending and forming it in the form of labyrinths, into which they threw themselves, and it swallowed them, and thus thrust them deep down under the earth there.
It appeared as if he had swallowed them.
